title: The TTF RF gap kernels, default `RfGapTTF` included, apply the particle phase correction with the wrong sign
summary: The default thin RF gap `RfGapTTF` delays the reference by Δφ₀ = qE₀Lκ(T′ sin φ + S′ cos φ)/(mβ²γ³), with E₀L the gap's field integral, φ its RF phase, κ = 2πf/(βc) and T′, S′ the κ-derivatives of the transit-time factors, but adds each particle's own correction Δφ to κz instead of subtracting it. A particle delayed more than the reference falls back, so κz must decrease by Δφ − Δφ₀, as direct integration through the field confirms. For a 2.5 MeV proton at 402.5 MHz, E₀L = 0.1 MeV and φ = −30°, the z→z map element is 1.009 instead of 1.001. The per-particle and three-point kernels share the error; the per-particle one grows the longitudinal phase-space area by 0.7903% per gap.

title: MAD RFCAVITY import uses VOLT in MV as GV and reverses the sign of the energy kick
summary: The TEAPOT factory behind `readMAD` turns an RFCAVITY into `RingRFTEAPOT` with the voltage unchanged and the phase φs = −2π·LAG; the node adds q·V·sin(2πhz/C + φs) GeV to dE, with h the harmonic number, C the ring length and z the distance ahead of the reference. VOLT is in MV, so it acts 1000 times too strong, and MAD's kick is VOLT·10⁻³·sin(2π·LAG − 2πhz/C) GeV, so the imported kick also has the wrong sign; the correct conversion is V = VOLT/1000 and φs = π − 2π·LAG. In a 10 m line, VOLT = 0.01 and LAG = 0.25 change the reference energy by −1.000×10⁻² GeV instead of +1.000×10⁻⁵ GeV. Below transition the sign alone makes a stable bucket unstable.

title: Per-particle TTF gap kernels move a particle that sits on the reference
summary: With `setLinacTracker(True)`, thin TTF gaps use `RfGapTTF_slow`, which evaluates each particle's transit-time factors and phase coefficient at its entrance velocity, while the reference particle uses the velocity at the gap midpoint. A particle with all six coordinates zero coincides with the reference and must leave the gap with zero z and zero energy deviation. For a 2.5 MeV proton in a 402.5 MHz gap with field integral E₀L = 0.1 MeV at φ = −30°, it leaves with ΔE = −0.1496 keV, 0.1962% of the 76.25 keV gain, and z = 5.731×10⁻⁷ m, at every gap. `RfGapThreePointTTF_slow`, used by axis-field gaps, gives the same kind of z offset; `BaseRfGap_slow` keeps the particle on the reference.

title: Axis-field RF gap phase solve stops one step before the gap centre
summary: `AxisFieldRF_Gap` finds the entrance phase that puts the reference at the cavity phase at the first gap's centre by stepping a test particle from the field start to the centre. When the accumulated position reaches exactly 0.0 in floating point, the loop exits one step early, so the solve matches the phase one step upstream and the gap runs off phase by about that step's transit phase. For a 2.5 MeV proton at 402.5 MHz, a −30° cavity phase and a field over ±10 mm in 1 mm steps, the reference crosses the centre at −23.41°; for ±20 mm at the default 10 mm step, at +36.03°. With 0.5 mm steps it crosses at −30.00°.

title: `RingRFTEAPOT` adds the synchronous energy gain to every particle's dE as well as to the reference
summary: `RingRFTEAPOT`, with voltage V, synchronous phase φs and harmonic number h in a ring of length C, raises the reference kinetic energy by q·V·sin φs and adds q·V·sin(2πhz/C + φs) to each particle's dE, but dE is measured from the reference, so the synchronous gain is counted twice. A particle on the synchronous orbit (z = dE = 0) must keep dE = 0; it instead gains q·V·sin φs on every pass and slides away from the bucket centre. With V = 10⁻³ GV and φs = 0.3 rad in a 10 m ring, it has dE = 2.955×10⁻⁴ GeV after one pass and 6.284×10⁻³ GeV with z = 9.029×10⁻² m after twenty. Stationary buckets (φs = 0) are unaffected.

title: A zero-strength TEAPOT quadrupole applies its kinetic correction on top of a full drift
summary: For kq = 0 or a neutral bunch, the TEAPOT quadrupole's linear step `quad1` falls back to the full nonlinear drift, but `QuadTEAPOT`, and the linac `Quad` with its default TEAPOT tracker, still apply the kinetic step `quad2`, whose terms complete the linear transport and so duplicate part of the drift. A switched-off quadrupole of length L therefore differs from a drift: at dE = 0 its path-length term doubles, Δz = −L(px² + py²) instead of −L(px² + py²)/2, and with η = dE/(p₀β₀) it adds Δx = −Lη·px/(1 + η). A 1 m quadrupole with kq = 0 gives z = −5.000×10⁻⁶ m for px = 10⁻³ and py = 2×10⁻³, where a drift, and a quadrupole with kq = 10⁻¹² m⁻², give −2.500×10⁻⁶ m.

confirmed.scope: neutral bunch and readMADX K1 = 0 extension

title: The linac tracker scales dipole corrector and thick-kicker kicks by each particle's momentum ratio
summary: With `setLinacTracker(True)`, linac dipole correctors and thick kickers call the linac `kick`, which multiplies the transverse kick by p₀/p_z, with p₀ the reference momentum and p_z the particle's longitudinal momentum. The linac tracker's transverse coordinates are pₓ/p₀ (its drift, quadrupole and RF gap maps all use this), and a field B_y over a length L changes pₓ by −qB_yL whatever the particle's momentum, so every particle must receive the node's kick −qB_yL/p₀ unchanged. A particle with relative momentum deviation δ instead receives (1 + δ)⁻¹ of it, 1.961% less at δ = +2%. The TEAPOT kick, used when the linac tracker is off, is exact.

title: The axis-field design pass tracks its first part with the previous design amplitude
summary: In `AxisFieldRF_Gap.trackDesign`, the first part of a cavity's first gap reads the cavity's design amplitude before the same call copies the current amplitude into it. The first design pass of a cavity whose amplitude is not 1.0, and the first pass after any amplitude change, therefore track that part with the old value (1.0 for a new cavity), while the phase solve and all later parts use the new one. For a 2.5 MeV proton at 402.5 MHz, a −30° cavity phase, field integral E₀L = 0.1 MeV and a uniform field over ±10 mm in 0.5 mm steps at amplitude 0.5, the first pass gains 34.18 keV and the next ones 34.28 keV, the value direct integration through the field gives.

confirmed.scope: first design pass of a new cavity

title: The three-point RF gap kernels skip a step whose centre field is zero
summary: `RfGapThreePointTTF`, the kernel of `AxisFieldRF_Gap`, fits E(s) = E₀(1 + as + bs²) through the fields at a step's start, centre and end, and returns without any kick when the centre field E₀ is zero, even when the end fields are not. The quadratic through those three points has a nonzero integral, and the kernel's energy gain has a finite limit as E₀ → 0. For a 2.5 MeV proton at 402.5 MHz, φ = −30° and a 10 mm step, end fields of 0 and 1 MV/m, as at the onset of a field, give no energy change instead of 1.768 keV, and end fields of 1 MV/m give none instead of 2.602 keV. The per-particle kernel behaves the same.

title: Ring RF nodes raise the reference energy without rescaling z, so an accelerating ring shrinks the longitudinal emittance by β₀,initial/β₀,final
summary: PyORBIT's longitudinal coordinate is z = −β₀cΔt, with β₀ the reference speed and Δt a particle's arrival time after the reference particle. The ring RF nodes that raise the reference energy (`RingRFTEAPOT`, the `orbit.rf_cavities` harmonic nodes driven by a synchronous phase or by a rigidity ramp, and `Frequency_RFNode`) change β₀ but leave z unchanged, so every particle's Δt is multiplied by β₀,in/β₀,out at each pass; the linac RF gaps apply the required z → z·β₀,out/β₀,in. Over a ramp the (z, dE) area is conserved instead of the (Δt, dE) area: accelerating protons from 50 to 200 MeV in a 100 m ring shrinks the rms (Δt, dE) emittance to 0.5547 of its initial value, β₀,initial/β₀,final, where a lab-frame tracker keeps it at 1.000.

title: Axis-field RF gaps drop part of the radial electric impulse, so their transverse map converges to a wrong limit as the step shrinks
summary: `AxisFieldRF_Gap` tracks an on-axis RF field E(s) as a series of thin transit-time kicks between drifts. Each kick keeps only the sin ψ part of the integrated radial impulse, ψ being the RF phase, and drops the boundary term −(x/2β)E cos ψ, nonzero between steps; summed over the steps it equals ½∫E cos ψ d(x/β), with x the offset and β the particle speed over c, and stays finite as the step shrinks. For a 2.5 MeV proton in a 402.5 MHz cos² field of ±10 mm with E₀L = 0.1 MeV at −30°, ∂pₓ,out/∂pₓ,in is 0.9928 of the Lorentz-force value at steps from 0.5 to 0.125 mm, and ∂pₓ,out/∂x_in 0.9821 to 0.9819. A static field gives no lens, where the exact ∂pₓ,out/∂pₓ,in is 1.0096.

title: The barrier RF cavity gives every species the energy kick of a unit positive charge
summary: `Barrier_RFNode` and `TimeDep_Barrier_RFNode` add their barrier waveform ±V·cos(π(φ − φ±)/(2Δφ±)) to each particle's dE without the bunch charge number q, with V the voltage in GV, φ the particle's RF phase and φ±, Δφ± the barrier centres and half-widths; the harmonic RF nodes, whose voltage is documented in the same words, add q·V. A particle of charge q crossing a voltage V gains q·V, so a q = −1 particle receives a proton's kick with the wrong sign, and a q = +28 ion 1/28 of its kick. For a 10⁻⁵ GV barrier and a particle 10° from the centre of the positive barrier, q = −1 gains +8.660×10⁻⁶ GeV instead of −8.660×10⁻⁶ GeV, and q = +28 gains 8.660×10⁻⁶ GeV instead of 2.425×10⁻⁴ GeV.

found.scope: barrier kernel for antiprotons and U²⁸⁺

title: The edge wedges of a combined-function bend scale their multipole kick by the bend length in metres
summary: In a TEAPOT or linac combined-function bend of length L with a nonzero face angle, the thin wedge between the sector body and the inclined face is kicked with the magnet's integrated multipole strength KₙL times the wedge length s, where the strength per length Kₙ gives Kₙ·s, so the wedge kick is L/(1 m) times its correct value. A 2 m bend with K₁ = 0.4 m⁻² and 0.1 rad faces must have the map of its two halves cut at a perpendicular plane, yet a ray at x = 10 mm leaves it 6.007 µm in x and 1.577 µrad in x′ away from them; passing KₙL/L makes them agree to roundoff. The error is second order in x, so linear optics are unaffected.

title: `Dual_Harmonic_Cav` evaluates the second harmonic at the fundamental's phase, so `RFPhase2` only adds a constant to every particle's energy
summary: `Dual_Harmonic_RFNode` and its kernel `Dual_Harmonic_Cav`, with fundamental voltage V, voltage ratio r, harmonic ratio n and phases φ₁ and φ₂, add q·V[sin φ − sin φ₁ − r(sin(φ₁ + n(φ − φ₁)) − sin φ₂)] to dE, φ being the particle's RF phase. Subtracting each harmonic's value at the synchronous phase φ₁ requires the second-harmonic wave sin(φ₂ + n(φ − φ₁)); with φ₁ in its place, φ₂ only adds q·V·r·sin φ₂ to every particle, and for φ₁ ≠ φ₂ the synchronous particle gains q·V·r(sin φ₂ − sin φ₁) per pass. For 1 GeV protons in a 100 m drift ring at harmonic number 1, V = 1 MV, n = 2, r = 0.25, φ₁ = 0 and φ₂ = 180°, the synchrotron tune is 0.003545, that of φ₂ = 0, instead of 0.006140.

title: `SynchPartRedefinitionZdE.shift_dE` and `center_dE` change the reference speed without rescaling z, which the default RF gap kernels read as an arrival time
summary: `SynchPartRedefinitionZdE.shift_dE(bunch, ΔK)` and `center_dE(bunch)` move the reference kinetic energy by ΔK, keeping each particle's energy and transverse momentum, but leave z unchanged while the reference speed β₀ changes. The default linac RF gap kernels read z as −β₀cΔt, with Δt the arrival time after the reference, so after the shift every particle's Δt is scaled by β₀,old/β₀,new and the next gap gives it the wrong energy; z·β₀,new/β₀,old is required. A 50 keV shift of a 2.5 MeV proton bunch shortens Δt by 0.9813%, and a following 402.5 MHz gap with E₀TL = 0.1 MeV at −90° gives a particle 5 mm ahead 476.4 eV more energy than without the shift. The per-particle kernels of the linac tracker are unaffected.

confirmed.scope: default gap kernels; not the linac tracker

title: The linac-tracker quadrupole drops the path lengthening of transverse slopes, so it does not reduce to the linac drift
summary: With `setLinacTracker(True)`, linac quadrupoles call `linac_quad1`, which advances z by (β − β₀)·L/β₀ with β the particle's total speed, β₀ the reference speed and L the step length. The longitudinal speed belongs there: a particle moving at slope θ = pₓ/p₀ travels a longer path and falls behind by about Lθ²/2, as the same tracker's drift and the TEAPOT quadrupole both give. The linac quadrupole therefore does not approach the drift as its gradient goes to zero. For 0.1 GeV protons through a 0.1 m quadrupole at θ = 3 mrad, z stays 0 at every gradient instead of −0.4500 µm at a vanishing gradient and −0.4353 µm at kq = 10 m⁻².

title: `BRhoDep_Harmonic_RFNode` stores the unstable synchronous position when the charge times the voltage is negative
summary: `BRhoDep_Harmonic_RFNode` stores as the synchronous z the position of the phase φs = arcsin(ΔEs/(qV)) below transition and π − arcsin above, with ΔEs the reference energy gain per pass, q the charge number and V the voltage, whatever the sign of qV. The cavity kick is qV sin φ, so for qV < 0 the stored z is the unstable fixed point. In a 248 m ring at 1 GeV with harmonic 4, 10 kV and q = −1, the stored z is +0.7329 m and the stable point −31.73 m; over 3000 turns a particle started 5 cm from the stored z runs 52.18 m away, one 5 cm from the stable point stays within 5.000 cm. The cavity kick and reference energy update are correct for either sign.

title: A weak TEAPOT solenoid loses the transverse positions through cancellation
summary: The TEAPOT solenoid kernel, used by `SolenoidTEAPOT` and the linac `Solenoid`, switches to a drift only for a strength |B| < 10⁻¹⁰⁰ m⁻¹, B being the field over the rigidity. For weaker strengths it recovers the positions by subtracting terms of size p⊥/B, with p⊥ the transverse momentum, so cancellation leaves a position error of about 10⁻¹⁶·p⊥/B. For a 1 GeV proton with x = 1 mm, pₓ = 1 mrad, y = 0.5 mm and p_y = 2 mrad through 1 m, x is off by 1.362×10⁻⁷ m at B = 10⁻¹² m⁻¹ and 3.830×10⁻⁵ m at 10⁻¹⁴ m⁻¹, and for |B| ≤ 10⁻¹⁷ m⁻¹ the particle leaves at x = y = 0 instead of 2.000 mm and 2.500 mm. At 10⁻⁸ m⁻¹ (56.57 nT) the error is 2.049×10⁻¹¹ m.

title: Linac RF gaps return NaN at the `RF_Cavity` default frequency of zero
summary: A linac `RF_Cavity` starts with frequency 0.0 Hz and amplitude 1.0, and nothing checks the frequency, so a hand-built lattice that never calls `setFrequency` tracks its gaps as active RF gaps at zero frequency. The default `RfGapTTF` divides by the frequency in its phase correction and in z = phase/κ, κ = 2πf/(βc): with E₀L = 0.1 MeV at 2.5 MeV the reference time and every particle's z become NaN, and the NaN time then makes x′, dE and z NaN after every later cavity, including a correctly set 402.5 MHz one. `BaseRfGap` gives NaN x′ and y′ for off-axis particles, the three-point kernels NaN everywhere, and the axis-field gap's design pass raises a `ValueError`. The same lattice at 1 mHz tracks finitely.

title: `getChromaticitiesXY` divides by the sine of the first-slice phase advance instead of the ring tune
summary: `TEAPOT_MATRIX_Lattice.getChromaticitiesXY` converts the energy derivative of the one-turn matrix trace into the chromaticity ξ = dν/dδ, with ν the betatron tune and δ the relative momentum deviation, by dividing by 2·sin(2πν). It takes ν from the second entry of the integrated phase-advance table, the phase advance ν₁ over the first slice of the lattice, instead of the ring tune, so the result is scaled by sin(2πν)/sin(2πν₁) and grows as the first slice gets shorter. For a six-cell quadrupole FODO ring with tunes 1.4753 it returns ξx = −18.62 instead of −1.830, the derivative of the tracked one-turn tune. For the SNS ring lattice shipped with the code it returns −97.36 instead of −7.548.

title: `getChromaticitiesXY` differentiates about the reference axis instead of the off-momentum closed orbit
summary: `TEAPOT_MATRIX_Lattice.getChromaticitiesXY` takes the energy derivative of the one-turn matrix from probe particles that start on the reference axis with an energy offset, not on the off-momentum closed orbit. With sextupoles and nonzero dispersion at the lattice start, the sextupole part of the chromaticity ξ = dν/dδ (ν the tune, δ the relative momentum deviation) then depends on where the lattice starts. In an eight-cell FODO ring with bends and thin sextupoles, and with the ring tune restored in the method's denominator, it gives ξx, ξy = 6.562, 6.641 when the ring starts at its first element and 9.578, 5.655 when it starts at its first bend. The closed-orbit tune derivative is 7.592, 5.978 at both starts.

title: `getRingParametersDict` reports no tunes for a stable coupled ring when one uncoupled block is unstable
summary: `MATRIX_Lattice.getRingParametersDict` judges stability from the two uncoupled 2×2 diagonal blocks of the transverse one-turn matrix and, when either has |cos μ| ≥ 1 (μ the phase advance), returns None for every tune, Twiss and dispersion entry, the coupled eigentunes included. With transverse coupling a diagonal block can have |cos μ| > 1 while all four eigenvalues of the 4×4 one-turn matrix lie on the unit circle, so the motion is stable and its eigentunes are defined. A four-cell FODO ring with a 1 m solenoid of strength kₛ = Bₛ/(Bρ) = 0.5 m⁻¹, Bρ the magnetic rigidity, has eigentunes 0.1530 and 0.4368 and x-block cos μ = −1.073; the method returns None for both, and `getTunes` raises TypeError.

title: `getTunes` adds a full turn for every negative-length element
summary: `MATRIX_Lattice.trackTwissData`, which `TEAPOT_MATRIX_Lattice.getTunes` and the ring phase-advance tables use, wraps each element's phase advance into [0, 2π) so that advances between π and 2π stay positive. This also turns the small negative phase advance of a negative-length element into almost 2π, so the integrated tune grows by one for every slice of such an element. Inserting a −0.3 m drift followed by a +0.3 m drift, whose product is the identity, into a six-cell FODO ring with tune 1.4753 raises `getTunes` to 2.4753, while the one-turn matrix and its fractional tune 0.4753 are unchanged. Lattices of positive-length elements are unaffected.
